task.description: WF-03 Step 2: design a fix relocating Letflow.Obs.Alerts.fire_hooks/4's deliver_with_retry/4 dispatch off Letflow.Scheduler.Poller's own process onto a new dedicated Task.Supervisor child in application.ex, per ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis (fixable now, no ISS-0425 dependency). Design only -- no implementation code.

result.summary: Design doc written at lib/letflow/design/iss0429-async-alert-hook-delivery.md. Key decisions: (1) new Task.Supervisor named Letflow.Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor, following the existing six domain-scoped Task.Supervisors' module-named convention, added to application.ex's flat children list positioned after Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistryTaskSupervisor and BEFORE the ++ scheduler_children() ++ http_child() tail -- this ordering IS load-bearing (unlike its order relative to the other six Task.Supervisors, which is not) because the Poller's first :tick fires with zero delay and would dispatch to this supervisor before it exists if ordered after scheduler_children(), mirroring SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor's own documented ordering hazard. (2) fire_hooks/4's call site changes from a direct synchronous deliver_with_retry/4 call to a Task.Supervisor.start_child/2 dispatch (fire-and-forget, not async_nolink + handle_info correlation) -- justified in the doc's §3 by showing alert delivery has no pool-slot-style bookkeeping or parked `from` to carry across an async boundary the way ISS-0224's SandboxPool fix needed, and that start_child/2 under a Task.Supervisor still gives crash observability via OTP's standard supervised-task crash-report/logging path, which is what avoids reintroducing ISS-0224's actual original hazard (a GenServer callback freezing its own mailbox) without needing async_nolink's monitored-result machinery. (3) check_and_record_emission/4 stays exactly where it is -- synchronous, on the caller, committed before dispatch -- preserving at-most-once/dedupe semantics unchanged; deliver_with_retry/4's body, @spec, backoff_delay/2, and RetryPolicy are all unchanged, now simply invoked from inside the dispatched Task instead of from the Poller. (4) maybe_run_alert_detection/3's existing try/rescue (poller.ex:153-157) needs NO code change -- its wall-clock duration shrinks dramatically but its structural purpose (isolate one schema's detection-and-dispatch pass) is unchanged, argued explicitly in §4. (5) webhooks.ex's identical-shape latent instance is explicitly out of scope, matching ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis. (6) Test approach (§6) specifies starting Poller's own GenServer directly (bypassing the start_scheduler: false gate for just that one test, async: false, sandbox mode adjusted for that test only, on_exit restores everything) to prove a second :tick is processed while a dispatched hook is still mid-backoff, plus a fail-first requirement against pre-fix code per WF-03 Step 4, plus a secondary unit-level Alerts test. One implementation-adjacent housekeeping item flagged in §7 (not a design ambiguity): alerts.ex's own moduledoc sections '## No new periodic process' and '## OQ-4 resolution' currently assert application.ex is unchanged and must be updated by ELIXIR-DEV since this fix does add a child.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to independently verify the design against ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis, confirm no implementation code is present, and confirm the application.ex ordering/naming/comment-convention requirements and the semantics-preservation claims (check_and_record_emission/4, backoff_delay/2, RetryPolicy) are each concretely specified rather than asserted.
